chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee', from Mansoor ibn Yunus, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who hires out himself, so he has banned the sustenance upon himself'.
And in another report, (He said): 'And how can he not have banned it, and whatever he acquires in it, so it is for his Lord who hired him'.

key_terms.حَظَرَ: to ban / to restrict / to withhold

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of hiring oneself out for work according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns against 'self-hiring' (ijarah al-nafs), a concept where one sells their time and labor exclusively for worldly wages, thereby neglecting spiritual duties and restricting divine rizq. The alternative narration clarifies that while the employer receives the physical labor, the true spiritual value and reward remain with God, emphasizing that ultimate sustenance is a divine gift rather than a mere transactional outcome. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing worldly livelihood with spiritual mindfulness, ensuring that work does not become an idol that displaces reliance on Allah.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Baize, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who hires out himself, so he has banned the sustenance upon himself’.
And in another report, (He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘And how can he not have banned it and whatever he acquires in it, so it is his Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Who has Recompensed him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Isma’il ibn Bazi’ from Mansur ibn Yunus from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar who has said the following:
“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ’One who offers himself for hire prohibits sustenance to himself .
5 In another Hadith it is said that how can it be anything other than prohibition when whatever one finds goes to his master? 5 ”
